summary: Gail Hinich Sutherland works in Indology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Chicago under advisers Carol Bolon and Wendy Doniger, and under traditional teacher Virendra Singh.

Galsan Gomboev (1822–1863) was a scholar in Iranian, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski and taught Mongolian at Saint Petersburg State University from 1855 to 1863.

Gananath Obeyesekere (1930–2025) studied at the University of Ceylon (B.A. ~1951–1955) and the University of Washington (M.A. ~1956–1958). He taught at Ceylon, Washington, UC San Diego, and Princeton University (1980–2000), working in religious and Buddhist studies.

Ganesh Prasad (1876–1935) studied at the universities of Allahabad and Calcutta. He headed a department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1905) and held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1917–1923) and the University of Calcutta (~1923–1935).

Ganganatha Jha (1872–1941) studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Calcutta, Allahabad, and Sanskrit College. Working in Indology and philosophy, he served at Muir Central College (1902–1918), Sanskrit College (1918), and as Vice-Chancellor of Allahabad University (1923–1932).
Gangs zhun is a Tibetologist who studied at Qinghai Nationalities Normal College (until 1989) and Northwest Minzu University (1998–2001), where he earned a master's degree under Alak Dorzhi Rinpoche.

Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Lama Byambaa and completed an M.Phil. in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under supervisor Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).
Garab Dorje Rinpoche (born 1967) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Thinley Norbu Rinpoche.

Garcin de Tassy (1794–1878) studied under de Sacy and Kieffer. A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he held the chair for Indian language at INALCO/École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1828–1878) and directed the Société Asiatique (~1876–1878).

Gareth Fisher works in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Ph.D. at the University of Virginia (2006) and served as Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology at Syracuse University (attested 2011–2016).

Gareth Sparham, a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, studied at McGill, the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and UBC (Ph.D. under Ashok Narhar Aklujkar). He later taught Tibetan language at the University of Michigan (1999–2009).

Gary A. Tubb (born 1950) is an Indologist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He has held teaching posts at Harvard (attested 1999), Columbia (attested 2007), and the University of Chicago (attested 2011, Emeritus 2026).

Gary D. DeAngelis works in religious and Buddhist studies. Mentored by Masatoshi Nagatomi, George Rupp, W. J. Johnson, Herbert Mason, and Daud Rahbar, he served as Associate Director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies at Holy Cross (attested 2017).

Gary Snyder (born 1930) studied at Reed, Indiana, and UC Berkeley under Shih-Hsiang Chen, plus Zen teachers Isshu Miura and Sesso Oda. Active in Buddhist studies and Japanology, he became a professor at UC Davis in 1986.

Gary Urton (born 1946) earned his degrees at the University of New Mexico and University of Illinois. Specializing in history and archaeology, he held positions at Colgate University (1978–2002) and Harvard University (~2002–2020), including department chair (2012–2018).
Gary Wee Kian Goh is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Hui-Chieh Loy, Jay L. Garfield, Brook Ziporyn, Christopher Anthony Brown, and Cecilia Lim.

Gaspare Gorresio (1808–1891) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Turin, under Eugène Burnouf, and under Stanislas Julien. He held Turin's chair of Sanskrit (1852) and directed the National University Library of Turin (1859).

Gaston Paris (1839–1903) was a linguist who studied under Friedrich Christian Diez and at the École des chartes. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1868–1903) and the Collège de France (1872–1903).
Gaston Renondeau (1879–1967) was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied at the École Polytechnique (~1898–1900).

Gaton Ngawang Lekpa (1864–1941) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and he taught Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima and Shenphen Nangwa.
